<result>## Assessment A: Reader and reply/compose design review (current main, after PR #29/#30)

**Evidence base:** this is a source, CSS, test and doc review only. Nothing was rendered. Geometry, contrast and look are inferred from the code. Mode: Operate (app UI).

### Design specificity
The surface is authored for this product, not category-interchangeable. Several details only make sense for an honest, local-only mail client:
- `Saved locally · not sent` (DraftEditorCore.vue:97-104).
- The real address beside the sender name in the collapsed To row (:144-149).
- Exact bytes next to the 5 MB limit (format-bytes.ts:26).
- Bidi-control stripping in file names.
- A lossless quote/signature split (message-body-format.ts).

The reader's layout is still pre-capture, and DESIGN.md gap 16 admits this. It is the least Superhuman-calibrated part of the app.

### Heuristics: 28/40 (Good)
This is up from 22-23. The inbox/search surface scores 35.

| # | Heuristic | Score | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Visibility of status | 3 | Single status line, quiet live region, honest loading skeleton. Cc and existing-draft state are invisible. |
| 2 | Match with real world | 3 | "Prepare reply" is internal vocabulary for what is a local draft. |
| 3 | User control | 3 | Esc, confirm on Discard, focus returns. "Cannot be undone" on Discard. |
| 4 | Consistency | 2 | Reader inset breaks from the list. Two reply glyphs. Inline "Save" vs chooser "Save to Downloads". |
| 5 | Error prevention | 3 | Address is never hidden; blocked-reply states are explicit. Blank drafts persist. |
| 6 | Recognition | 3 | `Prepare reply — R` in titles and palette; icon-only header glyphs. |
| 7 | Flexibility | 3 | R, N/P/O, Esc. No keys for quote, save or Cc/Subject. |
| 8 | Aesthetic and minimalist | 3 | Big gain. Worst-case notice stack and duplicate reply controls remain. |
| 9 | Error recovery | 3 | Retry, Save as new and Reload are honest. The attachment load failure has no retry control. |
| 10 | Help | 2 | Caveats sit behind an info button only. No reader key hints beyond titles. |

### Cognitive load: 2 of 8 fail (moderate, borderline good)
- **Visual hierarchy:** the subject is 16px/600 and the body is 15px/400, so weight does all the work.
- **Minimal choices:** the reader toolbar has 6-7 icon-only actions (back, done, read, files, reply, prev, next). The attachment chooser has more than 5 per decision.

Single focus, chunking, grouping, working memory and progressive disclosure pass. The docked composer keeps the thread visible.

### Emotional journey
The peak is good: R puts the cursor straight in the body. The end is flat. `Save and close` leaves a draft that can never be sent, with no handoff such as copy or open in the provider. That limit is honest, but it makes the loop end in Gmail.

### Strengths
1. One honest vocabulary for state, with detail in titles and hidden text instead of paragraphs.
2. Keyboard continuity: R, Esc, `takeFocus` and focus return are carefully guarded (DraftEditorCore.vue:190-225).
3. Restraint: no cards. The quote, signature and attachment lists are quiet and lossless.

### Priority issues
**P1 – R/Esc litters Drafts and shows no draft marker.**
- `openNew` persists a draft immediately (useDrafts.ts:475-506).
- `flushAndClose` has no pristine-blank cleanup (:454-460).
- Nothing in the reader or list shows that a reply draft exists. A second R mints a new envelope. I could not check whether core dedupes.
- Why: an R-then-Esc peek leaves blank drafts, which undermines trust in a triage loop.
- Fix: resume the draft for the same source, or drop a blank draft on close. Show `Draft` in the reader status line.
- Command: `harden`

**P2 – Reader geometry is off the product grid.**
- `.reader-pane` has `padding: .5rem .75rem` (style.css:1319-1323). The subject starts near 12px while the header title and list sit on the 50px inset.
- The undocked compose card uses the 50px margin (:2284); the docked one uses 0 (:2300).
- Why: opening a row visibly shifts the text edge, unlike the inbox.
- Fix: put the reader on the 50px inset and decide the right edge.
- Command: `layout`

**P2 – Reply heading and To can disagree.**
- The heading is always `Reply draft to {From name}` (ReplyComposer.vue:111).
- Core defaults To from Reply-To (generated.ts:426; draft_core.rs:376).
- When it differs, `toIsDefault` is false (DraftEditorCore.vue:135) and Cc/Subject auto-open (:159). The compact form is lost on list, newsletter and support-desk mail.
- Fix: derive the heading from `content.to`, or add a "Reply-To differs" line.
- Command: `clarify`

**P2 – Recipients look complete when they are not.**
- The Message DTO has no Cc. The reader shows `to X, Y` (ReaderView.vue:1017) and Details lists From, To and Sent only (:1050-1082).
- With no reply-all, a Cc'd thread silently drops people.
- The sender address needs Details or the contact pane, while the composer always shows it.
- Fix: show "Cc not cached", or fetch Cc.
- Command: `clarify`

**P2 – Type scale and quote parsing.**
- The reading size of 15px (style.css:27) is not in DESIGN's scale.
- Mono drops the text to 13.6px whenever any `>` line exists (message-body-format.ts:12-17, a documented limitation).
- The `ATTRIBUTION` pattern is English-only (:42), so "Le … a écrit :" quotes never collapse.
- Command: `typeset`

### Persona red flags
**Alex (power user)**
- No keys for Show quoted text, Save attachment or Cc/Subject, and no hints for N/P/O.
- R then Esc litters blank drafts.
- Nothing can finish a reply inside the app.

**Sam (accessibility)**
- Chooser buttons all read "Save to Downloads" (AttachmentChooser.vue:83), while the inline ones have per-file labels.
- Each `.participant` is a role-less `tabindex=0` span, which is an extra stop per recipient.
- The `▸` in Details is generated CSS (style.css:1641).
- Positive: the live region is quiet, and the full date is in hidden text.

**Riley (stress tester)**
- All messages render, with no cap or virtualization for 200 messages.
- `quotedSnippet` slices at 200 UTF-16 units (App.vue:441), which can split a surrogate pair, and previews the raw head rather than the prose.
- The attachment "Could not load file details." has no retry (MessageAttachments.vue:62).
- Up to 20 Reply-To recipients sit in one single-line input.

**Project persona (author triaging volume)**
- Replying is a dead end that ends in Gmail.
- Every R/Esc costs a Drafts row.
- The reader shows no unread or draft context per thread.

### Minor observations
- The skeleton row is `1.4em` (style.css:1418-1421) while its comment says the collapsed height is `2em`, so the pane may still jump.
- `.reader-pending` is not a status role.
- `describeError` leaks `invalid field:` (ReaderView.vue:204).
- The chooser's 230-character empty-state line (AttachmentChooser.vue:86) and the "Known files" jargon remain.
- The active-message lavender bar and the composer focus ring coexist, which is allowed by the focus-ring exception.

### Provocative questions
1. If a reply can never be sent, should R exist at all, or should it be "Open in provider" with the thread context?
2. Should the reader copy the list's quiet grammar, meaning no per-message bars, no rule lines and a 50px inset, rather than carry its own?
3. Is hiding the quote behind a toggle right for a user who replies by scanning the quote, or only for one who skims?

**Run notes:** nothing was rendered, so look and spacing are unverified. Contrast was not measured. Screen-reader behavior was not heard. I did not check whether core dedupes repeated reply drafts, how the native shell behaves, or any data beyond the fixtures. I did not run the detector or any tests.</result>

Method: dual-agent (A: design review, `afadc6012e007d725` · B: detector and deterministic checks, `a2b99a8ea0819d3c5`), run as isolated sub-agents. Both worked from source only, because there is no browser and no `node_modules`, so nothing was rendered. I haven't independently checked the file references below.

# Critique: reader and reply/compose, after PRs #29 and #30

## Design health: 28/40 (Good), up from 22

| # | Heuristic | Score | Key issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Visibility of status | 3 | Single quiet status line and honest loading skeleton. Cc and "a draft already exists" are invisible. |
| 2 | Match with real world | 3 | "Prepare reply" is internal vocabulary for what is a local draft. |
| 3 | User control | 3 | Esc, Discard confirm and focus return are solid. |
| 4 | Consistency | 2 | Reader sits off the product grid. Two reply glyphs. Inline "Save" vs chooser "Save to Downloads". |
| 5 | Error prevention | 3 | The real address is never hidden. Blank drafts persist. |
| 6 | Recognition | 3 | R is hinted in titles and the palette. Header glyphs are icon-only. |
| 7 | Flexibility | 3 | R, N/P/O and Esc exist. No keys for quote, save, or Cc/Subject. |
| 8 | Minimalist | 3 | Big gain. Worst-case notice stack and duplicate reply controls remain. |
| 9 | Error recovery | 3 | Retry, Save as new, Reload are honest. Attachment load failure has no retry. |
| 10 | Help | 2 | Caveats behind an info button only. No key hints beyond titles. |

The inbox and search surface is at 35. Cognitive load is moderate, with 2 of 8 checklist items failing:
- Visual hierarchy: 16px/600 subject against 15px/400 body, so weight does all the work.
- Minimal choices: the reader toolbar has 6-7 icon-only actions.

## Design specificity

The surface is authored for this product, not interchangeable. Examples:
- "Saved locally · not sent".
- The real address beside the sender name.
- Exact bytes next to the 5 MB limit.
- Bidi-control stripping in file names.
- A lossless quote and signature split.

The reader's layout is still pre-capture (DESIGN.md gap 16), and it is the least Superhuman-calibrated part of the app.

**Deterministic scan:**
- The six reader and compose `.vue` files returned zero findings.
- `style.css` returned 6 advisories, all outside the reader/composer ranges: three side-tab and three radius.
- No hardcoded colours and no off-scale font sizes in this area.
- Browser overlay was not run, so no overlay exists.

## What's working
1. **One honest vocabulary for state.** Detail moves into titles and hidden text instead of paragraphs.
2. **Keyboard continuity.** R, Esc, focus hand-off and focus return are carefully guarded, and the live region is quiet.
3. **Restraint.** No cards. Quote, signature and attachment lists are quiet and lossless.

## Priority issues

**[P1] R then Esc litters Drafts, and nothing shows a draft exists.**
- Why: opening a reply persists a draft immediately, closing has no blank-draft cleanup, and a second R may create another. A peek leaves blank drafts, which hurts trust in a triage loop. A could not check whether core dedupes.
- Fix: resume the existing draft for the same source, or drop a blank draft on close. Show "Draft" in the reader status line.
- Command: `harden`

**[P2] Reader geometry is off the product grid.**
- Why: `.reader-pane` uses 8px/12px padding, so the subject starts near 12px while the header and list sit on the 50px inset. Opening a row visibly shifts the text edge. The undocked compose card uses the 50px margin and the docked one uses 0.
- Fix: put the reader on the 50px inset and decide the right edge.
- Command: `layout`

**[P2] Recipients can look complete when they aren't.**
- Why: the heading is always "Reply draft to {From name}", but To defaults from Reply-To, so on list and newsletter mail the compact form is lost. The message data has no Cc, so a Cc'd thread silently drops people, and nothing says so.
- Fix: derive the heading from the actual To. Show "Cc not cached", or fetch Cc.
- Command: `clarify`

**[P2] Composer affordances are too faint, and some targets are tiny.** A and B agree here.
- Why: the field underline (Seam) is **1.36:1** on the raised surface, below 3:1, and it is the only at-rest cue that an empty field is an input. The caveat toggle is about 18×18px. Each `.participant` span is an extra tab stop whose focus shows only a colour change and dotted underline, not a ring. The chooser's buttons all read "Save to Downloads".
- Fix: raise the field cue to 3:1 or add a second cue. Enlarge the toggle's hit area. Give participants a real focus ring or drop the tab stop. Label chooser buttons per file.
- Command: `polish`

**[P2] Quote parsing and type scale.**
- Why: the attribution pattern is English-only, so "Le … a écrit :" quotes never collapse. Any interleaved `>` line still drops the whole body to 13.6px mono. The 15px reading size isn't in the DESIGN.md scale.
- Fix: broaden attribution matching, handle interleaved quotes, document `--type-reading`.
- Command: `typeset`

## Persona red flags
- **Alex (power user):** no keys for show quoted text, save attachment or Cc/Subject, and no hints for N/P/O. Replying ends in a draft that can't be sent.
- **Sam (accessibility):** per-recipient tab stops, weak participant focus, identical chooser labels. In their favour, the live region is quiet and the full date is in hidden text.
- **Riley (stress tester):** all messages render with no cap for a 200-message thread. The quote preview slices at 200 UTF-16 units and can split a surrogate pair. Attachment load failure has no retry.
- **The author triaging volume:** every R-then-Esc costs a Drafts row, and the reader shows no draft context per thread.

## Minor observations
- The skeleton row is 1.4em while its comment says 2em, so the pane may still jump.
- `describeError` leaks "invalid field:".
- The chooser has a 230-character empty-state line and "Known files" jargon.
- Up to 20 Reply-To recipients sit in one single-line input.

## Questions to consider
1. If a reply can never be sent, should R be "Open in provider" with the thread context?
2. Should the reader adopt the list's quiet grammar (no per-message bars, 50px inset) rather than its own?
3. Is hiding the quote right for someone who replies by scanning it?

Saving the snapshot now.

input.message:
Task: implement the fixes from an Impeccable critique of the reader and reply/compose UI of Email OS (Vue 3 + Tauri desktop email client), in five steps (layout, clarify, polish a11y/affordances, typeset, final polish). The critique scored the area 28/40 (was 22/40; inbox/search is 35/40). It was done from source only (no browser, no node_modules, nothing rendered), so VERIFY every claim by reading the code and reproducing it in a test before fixing; if a claim is wrong, say so and skip it.

Read PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md (read fully) first. Brand: focused, precise, trustworthy; keyboard-first; honest state; message content renders as safe literal plain text; drafts local-only; no Send by design; anti-references: Gmail clutter, AI magic, generic SaaS cards, optimistic UI that lies. Mode is Operate (app UI): consistency, density and native expectations outrank expression. The Impeccable skill is installed at ~/.claude/skills/impeccable (SKILL.md and reference/*.md; its launcher is ~/.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable). Use it: run `~/.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable context --target src/components/ReaderView.vue` once, then follow reference/layout.md, clarify.md, polish.md and typeset.md for the respective steps, and read reference/craft-floor.md immediately before editing UI. `impeccable detect --json <files>` is available for a deterministic scan (the reader/compose .vue files currently scan clean; style.css has 6 known pre-existing advisories outside this area). Ignore the 'CONTEXT_STALE' notes about PRODUCT.md/design.json drift; do not repair them. Also read the repo's `implement` skill / persona-feature-engineer agent and use it for implementation, test-first.

Out of scope: DRAFT INTEGRITY (the P1 about R then Esc leaving blank drafts / resuming drafts / a 'Draft' marker in the reader status line) is explicitly deferred; do not change draft creation, dedupe or cleanup behaviour. Also out of scope: a provider handoff / 'Open in provider' (local drafts stay as they are), the drawer panels (DraftsPanel, ActivityPanel, RemindersPanel, CachedTrashPanel; another thread, branch impeccable/drawer-panels, may be touching them and DraftsPanel embeds DraftEditorCore, so keep DraftEditorCore API-compatible and changes there minimal), AccountPanel/ProviderDestinations/first-run (another thread, impeccable/account-first-run), search, bulk selection bar/notice dock. Rebase on origin/main if conflicts appear; main has moved (reminders PR #33).

Steps, with findings (file:line refs are from the review; re-find them):

Step 2 LAYOUT (P2). Reader geometry is off the product grid. `.reader-pane` uses `padding: .5rem .75rem` (style.css ~1319-1323), so the subject starts near 12px while the header title and the inbox list sit on the 50px inset; opening a row visibly shifts the text edge. The undocked compose card uses the 50px margin (~2284) but the docked one uses 0 (~2300). Put the reader on the 50px inset (decide the right edge deliberately and keep long-line measure at 65ch), make docked/undocked compose margins agree, and fix the loading skeleton row height (style.css ~1418-1421 uses 1.4em while its comment says the collapsed height is 2em, so the pane may still jump). Keep J/K reader navigation smooth with no empty frame. Reconcile DESIGN.md gap 16 and the reader geometry docs.

Step 3 CLARIFY (P2). (a) The reply heading is always `Reply draft to {From name}` (ReplyComposer.vue ~111), but To defaults from Reply-To (generated.ts ~426; draft_core.rs ~376), so on list/newsletter/support-desk mail the heading and the To row disagree and Cc/Subject auto-open (DraftEditorCore ~135, ~159). Derive the heading from the actual To (or add a terse 'Reply-To differs' line) and verify the compact form still holds when Reply-To differs. (b) The Message DTO has no Cc: the reader shows `to X, Y` (ReaderView ~1017) and Details lists From/To/Sent only (~1050-1082), so a Cc'd thread looks complete and a reply silently drops people. Say so plainly and tersely, e.g. 'Cc not cached' where Cc is unknown; do not fabricate Cc and do not change the wire format unless trivial and safe. (c) Replace the internal 'Prepare reply' wording with plain 'Reply' in titles, labels, palette and tests, keeping the R hint. (d) `describeError` leaks `invalid field:` (ReaderView ~204): replace with a plain message. (e) AttachmentChooser empty state is a ~230-char line (AttachmentChooser.vue ~86) and uses 'Known files' jargon: shorten to terse factual copy. Voice: terse, factual, sentence-case, no exclamation marks.

Step 4 POLISH: affordances and accessibility (P2). (a) The composer field underline (Seam #474543) is 1.36:1 on the raised surface and is the only at-rest cue that an empty field is an input; raise it to >=3:1 or add a second at-rest cue, staying within DESIGN.md tokens (add a token only if needed and document it). (b) `.composer-caveat-toggle` is ~18x18px; enlarge the hit area (not necessarily the glyph). (c) `.participant` spans in the reader (ReaderView ~1054, ~1071) are role-less `tabindex=0` with a colour-only/dotted-underline focus style and add a tab stop per recipient: either give them a real visible focus ring and a role, or remove the extra tab stops (the full address must stay reachable by keyboard and screen reader). (d) AttachmentChooser buttons all read 'Save to Downloads' (~83): give each a per-file accessible label like the inline ones. Align inline 'Save' vs chooser 'Save to Downloads' wording. (e) MessageAttachments 'Could not load file details.' (~62) has no retry: add a Retry action. (f) The `▸` in Details is generated CSS (style.css ~1641): make sure state is exposed to assistive tech (aria-expanded or native details semantics). Do not use Graphite (#8e8a87) for meaningful glyphs on focus-fill (2.75:1). Keep every existing live region quiet (status line announces only meaningful transitions).

Step 5 TYPESET (P2). (a) The quote attribution pattern is English-only (message-body-format.ts ~42), so 'Le ... a écrit :' / 'Am ... schrieb ...' / 'El ... escribió:' etc. quotes never collapse: broaden it safely (still plain text, lossless, no HTML), with tests. (b) Any interleaved `>` line in the prose forces the whole body to monospace at 13.6px (message-body-format.ts ~12-17, documented limitation): fix if small and safe (e.g. only force mono when the non-quoted prose itself looks tabular/aligned), otherwise keep the limitation and document it. (c) The 15px reading size (`--type-reading`, style.css ~27) is not in DESIGN.md's scale: document the reading type role (size, line-height 1.6, 65ch measure, mono fallback) in DESIGN.md. (d) Review hierarchy in the reader: 16px/600 subject over 15px/400 body leans on weight alone; adjust only if a measured, small change fixes it, otherwise leave and say why. (e) quotedSnippet slices at 200 UTF-16 units (App.vue ~441), which can split a surrogate pair and previews the raw head; slice by code points/grapheme boundary.

Step 6 POLISH final. Run the detector on the touched files, a CSS hygiene pass (no hardcoded colours, tokens only, on-scale spacing/radii, focus-visible on every new interactive element), re-check DESIGN.md/docs for claims that changed, make sure nothing from steps 2-5 regressed editable/IME shortcut protection, announcements, focus handling, reduced-motion or J/K smoothness. Minor leftovers to fold in if trivial: `.reader-pending` should be a status role; chooser 'Known files' jargon; up to 20 Reply-To recipients in a single-line input (check layout only).

Constraints: honour PRODUCT.md 'Standing constraints'; no HTML rendering of message content; no auto-open of attachments; no optimistic UI; no real provider writes. Copy terse, sentence-case.

Process: run `pnpm install` if node_modules is missing, then add failing tests first for each verified issue, fix, and run the project's checks (see mise.toml and docs/development.md; lint, typecheck, vitest). Commit per step with clear messages on this branch, update DESIGN.md/docs where behaviour or claims changed, add a short note to the reader/compose critique files under .impeccable/critique/ (create a new file in the existing format if the previous ones are not on your branch), and open ONE PR to main. Report back: what you changed per step, what you verified and how, what you rejected or could not verify (e.g. no rendered screenshots; say whether you were able to run the app or take any), and anything deferred.
